rows.en:
One day, after P.E. class ended, he suddenly needed to go.
It beat wetting himself, so he went there, since he had no choice.{p}

The restroom was chilly, and the whole wall was covered with that letter board.
He'd heard the rumors, but this was the first time he'd ever really looked at it.{p}

Then one day, a few days later.
It was during lunch break.{p}

I'd eaten my lunch and gone up to the roof, and there in a corner was Tsuda, eating his lunch all alone.
Tsuda was a light eater, you see.
He always ate like the food tasted awful.
For me, mealtime is the happiest time of all.
Tsuda was the complete opposite.
It looked like he forced himself to eat because he had to.
But guess what?
That time, he was wolfing it down like a different person.
He was shoveling the food from his lunch box into his mouth at a tremendous pace.
I waved and walked over to him.{p}

"Hey, Tsuda!"
Tsuda only glanced at me for a second; the hand holding his chopsticks never stopped for a moment.
Was he eating something that delicious?
If so, maybe I'd ask him for one too, I thought as I got closer...
I almost threw up what I'd just eaten.
What he was eating were baby mice.
His lunch box was heaped with baby mice.
The raw pink kind that hadn't grown any fur yet.
He knew I was right next to him, but he kept eating, completely absorbed.{p}

Then, when he'd polished off the whole lunch box full of baby mice, he wiped his mouth with a very satisfied look and sighed.
And then he looked at me.
"What's wrong, Hosoda?"
He said it as if he found it strange that I was standing there frozen.
Then he closed the lid of his lunch box, walked past me, and went back downstairs.{p}

I couldn't move for a while.
Even now, I can't forget the way he looked at me.
His pupils seemed to be slit vertically, like a cat's eyes.
After that, I decided to stay away from Tsuda.{p}
One day after school, I saw him tottering off toward the back of the gym.{p}If it were you, {a}{f:|}, would you try following him?
Follow him
Don't follow him

Curious, I followed him, though I should have known better.
Maybe I could find out what had made him change.
Right now he was just a creep, but he'd been my friend, after a fashion...
That's what I thought.{p}

I followed him, and the place he went was that restroom.
I quietly watched him from the shade of a tree.{p}

At that point, it was still more of a strange sight than a scary one.
It was dusk, and a few big moths had gathered around the fluorescent light in the dim restroom.
He deftly caught those moths in his mouth and started eating them.
There must have been several moths, and it looked like he ate every last one.
Watching that sight the whole time made me feel sick.
Which, I suppose, is only natural.
"Bleeeeegh!"
I threw up right there, hard.
Thinking he might have heard me, I quietly looked over at the restroom.{p}
And he wasn't in the restroom anymore.{p}

I had a bad feeling and turned around, and there he was, staring at me with glowing cat-like eyes.
"...You saw."
That voice wasn't his.
Then, while I was frozen by the suddenness of it all, he lunged at me.
He knocked me down and straddled my chest.
Then, with his mouth still coated in powder from the wings of the moths he'd just eaten, he licked my face, all the way up.
On reflex, I pressed the charm I always carry against his forehead.{p}

"Gyaaaagh!"
He let out a tremendous scream and collapsed with a thud.{p}
When he collapsed, I saw something like a white mist leave him and drift toward the restroom wall.{p}

And then it vanished, as if it had been sucked into the letter board.
I saw it.
It was definitely shaped like a white fox.
"Tsuda☆"
I shook Tsuda, lying there, until he woke up.{p}

"Hosoda?
What's going on?
Why am I here?"
Tsuda seemed to be thinking for a while.
Then he said this to me.
"...You know, I don't remember anything from the past few days.
What happened to me?
I went to that restroom beside the gym, and I don't remember anything after that.
And when I came to, I was here.
Weird, huh?"
Prompted by his words, I found myself nodding.
And I kept quiet about all the strange things he'd been doing.
I mean, I didn't think Tsuda would believe me even if I told him.
I think Tsuda was probably possessed by that fox.
Of course, I didn't tell him that either.
Well, Tsuda was back to normal, after all.
Case closed, as they say.
Tsuda still comes to school like normal, even now.
Alive and well.{p}
Hey, {a}{f:|}.{p}You're not going to tell me you want to see that restroom's letter board, are you?
I want to see it
I don't want to see it
If you want to see it, {a}{f:|}, I'll show you the way.{p}

Okay, here we are.
This is the restroom.
{f:Hosoda and I|Hosoda and I} stepped into the dim restroom.
The cold, clammy air clung to my cheeks.{p}

"This is the letter board..."
Hosoda pointed at the board.
Sure enough, the letters on the board were grimy, {f:but|but} I could still read them clearly{f:.|.}
Over the letters were dark stains, like blackened blood.
"{a}{f:|}☆
Look☆"
Hosoda pointed at the board again.{p}

There, stuck fast to the wall with the letter board, was a ten-yen coin crusted with blue-green rust.
"What's going on{f:|}★"
{f:We|We} couldn't move from that spot, as if we were held by an invisible force.
Then, unbelievably, the ten-yen coin began to glide across the board on its own.{p}

"WHAT HAVE YOU COME HERE FOR"
The coin spelled it out.
"We were just passing by."
{f:I|I} said.
"What do we do?
Kokkuri-san came down on its own!
We have to get it to go back, fast!"
Hosoda said in a panic.{p}

"DO NOT LIE"
The coin spelled it out again.
Cold sweat trickled down my back.
{f:We|We} were truly terrified now.{p}
Ask Kokkuri-san to go back
Run away

"Please, Kokkuri-san.
Please, go back where you came from.
I'm begging you!"
Hosoda pleaded, his voice on the verge of tears.{p}

"Let's {f:run|run}!"
{f:I|I} shouted.{p}
Just then, the restroom's entrance door slammed shut.
"Oh no!"
Push or pull, the door wouldn't open.{p}

{f:We|We} turned around.
The ten-yen coin had started moving again.{p}

"YOU WILL NOT ESCAPE. I WILL KILL YOU"
The ten-yen coin moved quietly.
If only {f:I|I} hadn't gotten curious back then...
...But it's too late now.{p}

But... I regret it.
Tsuda hanged himself in there, just like that boy who loved fortune-telling.
His fingertips were bleeding.
Apparently he'd cut his own fingertips and traced over that letter board with the blood.
They say that to the people who saw it, for a moment it looked as if blood was flowing out of the letter board itself.
I never, ever go to that restroom.
You must never go there either, {a}{f:|}.
I don't know what happened to him in there...
If I'd followed him back then... maybe, just maybe, I could have saved him.
Then again, with bad luck, I might have died too.
...And that's the end of my story.
I wonder when the seventh person will get here.
If they don't come, the next one will be the last.
I wonder what kind of story it'll be this time.{p}

That's good.
I was worried about what I'd do if you said you wanted to see it, {a}{f:|}.
I was only asking as a joke, though.
...That's the end of my story.
Well then, let's move on to the next one.
If the seventh person doesn't come, this will be the last one.{p}

That's for the best.
No way is anyone's own life that easy to figure out, I tell you.
It's just a comfort.
I believe in spirits, but I don't believe in fortune-telling.
Though if you use spirits to tell fortunes, that's another story.{p}

You're saying you're not interested?
Well, if you're not interested, it can't be helped.
I guess hearing the story wouldn't be any fun for you at all.
Fine, fine.
Then I'll just stop telling the story right here.
That'll make you happy, right?
Even though the spirits might have been listening to this story too.
If I stop partway through, I bet the spirits will be left frustrated, don't you think...?{p}

Don't blame me, okay?
It's because you said you weren't interested, {a}{f:|}.
...And that's the end of my story.
...The seventh person still isn't here.
That means the next one will finally be the last.
I hope nothing happens, {a}{f:|}.{p}

"We did it! Now, let's get out of here!"
Hosoda grabbed {f:my|my} hand and started running.{p}

You got it.
That's amazing. So you're sensitive to spirits haunting restrooms too, {a}{f:|}.
I had a feeling you were the same type of person as me, {a}{f:|}.
That's right, that place is haunted by the spirits of fish.
Strange, isn't it?
Fish spirits, in a restroom.
Anyway, about the reason that restroom stopped being used.{p}

Once upon a time, there was a boy at this school.
Unfortunately, I don't know his name.{p}

Now, this school has a pond in the courtyard, right?
There are all kinds of creatures in it, turtles and koi and goldfish and so on.{p}{a}{f:|}, do you dislike fish, or things like that?
I like them
I dislike them

I see.
Liking living creatures is a good thing.
They're cute, aren't they? Goldfish and turtles and all.
I keep tropical fish and a green turtle at home too.
I just can't understand people who say they hate fish.{p}

Getting back to the story, he hated living creatures.
Throwing stray cats in the river, hurling stones at dogs... he did the kind of things little brats do, without a second thought, even though he was in high school.
That's right, and so the fish in that pond fell victim to him too.
He'd take the fish out of the pond one at a time and do horrible things, like poking them with a stick until their guts came out, or roasting them over a fire and feeding them to cats.
It seems he enjoyed it more than anything.
The courtyard pond is wide and deep, so apparently there were quite a lot of creatures in it, and even with him taking them, nobody noticed.{p}

Yes, and the place where he tormented those fish was that restroom beside the gym.
If the fish he killed weren't too big, he could just flush them down the toilet as they were, so it was pretty convenient for him.
Somehow, that restroom became like a torture chamber for fish.
Eventually a friend who couldn't stand to watch it told him to stop, but he wouldn't listen to a word of it.{p}

And then he started researching crueler ways to kill them.
He'd try jabbing insect pins into both of a fish's eyes, or stick pins all over its body and go,
"Now you're a porcupinefish."
That's the kind of thing he'd say.
Or he'd try soaking goldfish in bleach.
One time, he caught a turtle, shoved its legs into its shell, wrapped it round and round with wire, and roasted it from underneath with fire.
The turtle tried to struggle, but because of the wire, it couldn't get its legs out.
Little by little, the fire scorched its shell.
After a sound like a scream, a long squeeeee, the turtle didn't struggle anymore.
"Suffer more!
Struggle harder!"
He shouted.
As if he had a grudge against the fish.
The helpless fish put up their tiny resistance and soon died.{p}

And then, at some point, a strange smell started hanging around that restroom.
Not the ammonia smell you get in restrooms, but something more rotten, more burnt.
You'd think it was the smell of fish corpses left lying around, right?
But he disposed of the fish corpses properly, so that wasn't the cause.
And the girls' restroom and the boys' restroom both had the same smell.
So bad that an ordinary person couldn't even step inside anymore.
Because of all that, fewer and fewer people used that restroom.
The teachers heard the rumors and checked it several times, but they found nothing that could be causing the smell.{p}

He loved that foul smell.
Because he felt like it made his heart even crueler...
And his torture of the fish went on as always.
At first he was satisfied with just small fish, but gradually he started to want to torment bigger ones.
And then he made up his mind.
Yes, he decided to catch the brocade koi they called the lord of that pond.{p}

He decided to carry out his plan on the evening of the coming Sunday.
The koi was used to people, so catching it was easy.
But it was so big that after scooping it into a net and hauling it out, he tied it up with string and carried it over his shoulder.
And he took it to that restroom.{p}
Flopping around inside the restroom, the koi looked to him as if it were begging, "Please torment me."{p}How do you think he tormented the koi?
Punishment: strip its scales and salt it
Punishment: slice it up alive as sashimi

"Ooh, there, there.
You want me to torment you that badly?"
He said it with a smirk.
Then he pinned the koi down with his foot and peeled off its scales one by one.
Each time, the koi gave a short twist of its body.
Each time, he felt the height of bliss.
"Does it hurt?
I bet it hurts.
Well then, how about this?"{p}

Writhing from the heat of the wax, the koi flopped so hard it fell into the toilet bowl.
"Well, isn't that just perfect?
Here you go, here you go..."
He took a handful of salt from a bag and sprinkled it over the koi.{p}

Stripped of its scales and doused with salt on top of that, the koi thrashed wildly.
It splashed toilet water all over him.
"What the hell☆
That's filthy.
Time for your punishment☆"
He turned the bag of salt in his hand upside down and dumped all of it on the koi.{p}

"Squeeeee..."
went the koi, as if screaming, and then it stopped moving.{p}
Then he chopped the koi into small pieces with a knife and flushed them down the toilet along with the scales.{p}

With a gurgling sound, the scraps of koi flesh washed away...
He left the restroom, very satisfied.{p}

Inside the restroom, there was only that strange smell; nothing in particular had changed.
Then he suddenly noticed a single scale stuck to his hand.{p}
Wondering if there might still be scales lying around the restroom, he washed his hands at the sink.{p}

And guess what? Those scales came gushing out of the faucet, mixed in with the water.
He yanked his hands back, but it was too late.
His hands were caked with scales.
He tried brushing them off, he tried shaking his hands, but the scales wouldn't come off.
Then, without thinking, he glanced at the mirror over the sink.{p}

"Aaaaaaagh!"
He screamed.
Because his whole face was covered in scales, packed tight.
The very same scales he'd torn off that koi the day before...
And on the side of his neck, a fish's gills were flapping open and shut.
By then, he couldn't make a sound anymore.
All you could hear was the wheezing whistle of gills breathing.
And webbing had grown between his fingers...{p}

Later, they say he was found hanged in that restroom.
And when they found him, he looked just like he used to, no scales, no gills...
Was he just seeing things...?
Ever since then, they say scales still turn up on the floor of that restroom every now and then.
Feeling sick?{p}Don't want to hear any more?
I don't want to hear it
Tell me the rest

You don't want to hear it?
I see. It's pretty gross, after all.
If you don't want to hear it, that's fine by me.
I'll just tell you this much: you'd better not go near that restroom.
Whatever happens, I'm not taking any responsibility, okay?
That's the end of my story.{p}

I really wanted to tell you more, though...
Oh well. If the seventh one doesn't show up, the next story is the last.{p}
Huh, so you don't like them.{p}

What? But you like eating fish?
Oh, okay, I get it.
You don't like them as pets, but you like them as food.
You're a practical one, aren't you, {a}{f:|}?{p}

"Aww, there, there.
You want me to torment you that badly?"
He said it with a grin.
Then he pinned the koi down with his foot and peeled off its scales one by one.{p}

"Squeeeeeee!"
The koi let out a sound like a scream.
Of course he couldn't carve up a koi as neatly as a real chef.
By the time he'd pulled out its guts and cut into its back, the koi had stopped moving.
That was when he learned something for the first time.
When a koi gets that big, it bleeds red blood, just like a human...{p}
In a rage, he hacked the koi in front of him to shreds.{p}

Then he flushed the chunks of koi flesh down the toilet.
He'd thought it would give him more fun than that... A little let down, he left the restroom.{p}

You want to know what happens next, huh?
All right, I'll tell you.
After what happened, nobody used that restroom anymore.
There was no point leaving a restroom nobody used just sitting there, so they decided to tear it down.
But when they called in contractors to demolish it... bad things happened.
Everyone involved in the work, they say, was tormented by nightmares.
In the dream, scales and gills and webbing grew all over their bodies.
One night would've been bad enough, but it went on for days.
And it happened to every single person involved.
They all got scared to sleep, and on top of that, none of them could eat fish anymore.
So the work was called off.{p}

I said scales still turn up in that restroom now and then, right?
If you ever see one, don't touch it, whatever you do.
Apparently your skin swells up like scales wherever it touches.
...And so, that's the end of my story.
Still, the seventh one sure is late.
I wonder what happened.
I hope nothing bad's happened.
Well then, shall we hear the next story?{p}

Oops, too bad.
Actually, it was a tanuki.
Well, to people like us, a tanuki and a fox are pretty much the same thing, right?
Anyway, about why that restroom stopped being used.{p}

A long time ago, there was a tanuki at this school.
Not that anybody kept it in the animal hutch or anything.
This school's right in the middle of the city, but somehow a tanuki wandered in.
So everyone thought it was a rare sight, and they made a fuss over it.
Every day, around lunch break, it would come out into the back courtyard to get fed.
I mean, animals are cute, right?
Everyone was happy to share their lunches with it.
But after a while, they got bored of it.
Nobody paid it any attention anymore.{p}

But there was one.
One student who kept taking care of it.
Unfortunately I don't know his name, but he was a boy.
He fed it every single day.
He even gave it a name.
I don't know what the name was, so let's just call it Ponkichi.
Ponkichi got really attached to him, too.
But if a teacher found out, he'd be in trouble, right?
Our school's especially strict about animals like that.
They say they bring fleas and lice and stuff.
So he thought it over.
If it kept coming out every day somewhere this visible, a teacher was bound to find it sooner or later.{p}

He built a nest box inside one of the stalls in the boys' restroom and had Ponkichi live there.
"Sorry, it smells a little, but please put up with it.
And I'm going to put a lid on so you don't wander off. You can put up with that, right?"
With that, he stretched netting over a cardboard box, rigging it so Ponkichi couldn't sneak out and roam around during class.{p}
That day, too, he wolfed down his lunch early, took the leftovers, and hurried off to Ponkichi.{p}

"Sorry I'm late. You must be hungry, huh?"
He said it as he walked into the restroom, and then the shock was so great that he dropped his lunch box.{p}
What do you think happened?{p}

Believe it or not, Ponkichi was dead.
To be precise, Ponkichi had been killed.
Here's how it started.
It was during classes that morning.
A certain student was skipping class and loafing around near that restroom.
He heard an animal crying from somewhere, and, curious, he searched inside the restroom.{p}

He found Ponkichi right away.
"What the hell is this thing..."
He wasn't especially interested in tanuki, but he took it out of the box anyway, just because.
Ponkichi thrashed and tried to get away.
Not about to let go of his new toy, he held on to Ponkichi tight.
Then Ponkichi bit down on his finger with a 'chomp!'{p}
"Ow! You little bastard!"{p}

He slammed Ponkichi onto the floor.
Slipping out of his hands, Ponkichi tried to run.
"Get back here, you little bastard!"
He hurried and grabbed Ponkichi.
"Don't think you're getting away."
He gripped Ponkichi firmly and hugged it to his chest, careful not to get bitten again.{p}

"All right, you're gonna be my toy.
I'm gonna kill some time with you, nice and slow.
Brace yourself."
With that, the guy started tormenting Ponkichi.{p}What do you think he did to Ponkichi?
Water torture
Burning at the stake
Torn limb from limb
Paraded through town, crucified, then the head put on display

"All right, I sentence you to be torn limb from limb."
With that, he tied Ponkichi to a pillar so it couldn't escape and started tormenting it.
"First, we split your legs."
The guy grabbed Ponkichi's hind legs and yanked them apart as hard as he could.
The hip joints shattered, and the legs dangled limply.
"Heh heh heh heh heh. What a sweet sound...
Now the front legs."
With that, he grabbed Ponkichi's front legs this time and yanked them apart the same way.
"Hee hee hee hee hee.
The way it shakes right through my hands, I love it..."
What a horrible guy, huh?
I bet his face looked just like a demon's right then.{p}

With its leg joints shattered, Ponkichi couldn't run away. It couldn't even writhe.
"Now, what should I do with you next?
I want to feel more bones crunch...
If I wring your neck, though, you'd die for sure..."{p}

The way he saw it, the fun was in tormenting a tanuki while it was still alive.
He had no intention of killing it quickly.
He went and got one of the concrete blocks stacked outside and brought it down as hard as he could on the hind legs hanging slack and limp.
"Hmm, that's not much fun.
Nowhere near as good as how it felt before..."
Its hind legs crushed, Ponkichi wept tears from the unbearable pain, twitching in spasms.{p}

"Huh, so tanuki cry too...
That's funny.
I'm gonna make you cry some more."
He tried this and that, and finally found a method that worked.
Tearing out Ponkichi's fur.
When he grabbed a tuft and ripped it out as hard as he could, tears streamed from Ponkichi's eyes.
He kept at it until there was no fur left on Ponkichi's back.
"Man, I'm starting to get bored.
If I leave it like this, it'll probably die anyway..."
Saying that, he grabbed Ponkichi by the neck and wrung it as hard as he could.
"Heh heh heh... That feels good..."
At last, Ponkichi stopped moving altogether.
Then he tossed Ponkichi into the cardboard box and walked out, just like that.{p}

Afterward, the boy who'd been taking care of Ponkichi found it.
He was heartbroken.
"Who would do something so cruel..."
Wanting at least to give it a grave, he made one beside that restroom and buried it there.{p}

Then a few days went by.
All that time, he never once missed visiting the grave.{p}

That day after school, too, he went over to the restroom to visit the grave.
And there was someone wrecking the grave.
Furious, he ran right up to the guy.
"What are you doing?!"
He confronted him, his face bright red.
But the guy got angry instead and punched him.
And then he said,
"I'm the one who killed the tanuki."
Just like that.
When he heard that, he went at the guy with his fists.
But he was no match for him at all.{p}

Instead, he got beaten to a pulp and dragged into the restroom.
The guy must have figured he'd beat him all he liked, where no one could see.
And he kept on beating him.
So much that the whole restroom ended up covered in blood.{p}

After that, he stayed home from school for several days until the swelling went down.
When he went back, everyone was talking about one particular boy.
Apparently that student had fallen off a station platform on his way home from school and been run over by a train.
They say his body was torn into pieces, and it was really gruesome.{p}

And, as it turned out later, that student was apparently the one who'd killed Ponkichi.
Scary, huh?
By coincidence, he ended up dying the same way Ponkichi did.
But to me, it doesn't seem like a coincidence at all.
I think there's something more to it.
What do you think, {a}{f:|}?{p}

So, about the restroom next to the gym.
Apparently, it's haunted.
By the ghost of that guy who got torn to pieces.
That ghost goes,
"It's your fault I ended up like this,"
muttering it over and over, they say.
Everyone wondered why it would haunt a place like that.
But either way, it was haunted all the same, so everyone got creeped out and stopped using that restroom.{p}
Actually, there's more to this story. Do you want to hear it?
No, that's enough
Please tell me more

All right.
Then I'll tell you the rest.{p}

The boy who'd been taking care of Ponkichi, see, he figured something out.
That it must have been Ponkichi getting revenge.
It made him feel a whole lot better.
After that, the days went by without anything happening.{p}

"Is someone there?"
But there was no one in the restroom.
(That's weird.)
The moment he thought that...{p}

It showed up.
He couldn't believe it.
The guy who'd killed Ponkichi was standing beside a stall door.
"It's your fault I'm dead.
Your fault... your fault..."
Saying that, the ghost lunged at him.{p}

And at last, he was cornered inside a stall.
"Help! Somebody, heeeelp!"
No matter how much he screamed, there was no sign of anyone coming.
(It's over...)
It was right as he thought that{p}

that he saw Ponkichi appear behind him...
"P-Ponkichi..."
(You came to save me!)
Thinking that, he felt relieved.
But that was a huge mistake.{p}

Sure, thanks to Ponkichi, the ghost went away.
I bet that ghost took one look at Ponkichi and ran off.{p}

After that, he started acting strangely.
Not so you'd notice if you just glanced at him, though.
In fact, even his friends in class didn't notice at first.
What was he doing, you ask?
Well, every lunch break, he'd disappear.
Without even eating his lunch.
Every break, he'd take his lunch box and go off somewhere.{p}

And when he came back, his lunch box was completely empty.
His classmates just assumed he was eating his lunch somewhere.
But during the next class, his stomach was always growling.
As if he hadn't eaten a thing.{p}

At first, everyone made fun of him.
Still hungry after eating your lunch? they said.
But as the days went by, he got thinner and thinner, wasting away.
A friend who was worried about him followed him to see where he went at lunch break.{p}

And it turned out he was going to the hill behind the old school building.
He went to a certain spot, and instead of eating his lunch, he was throwing it away.
The friend went up to talk to him, meaning to ask why he was doing that.
And the friend was shocked.
His face had changed.
That's right, it looked like a tanuki's face.
The friend warned him.
Don't throw your lunch away. Eat it, or you'll die.
But he wouldn't listen.
He said these guys needed to eat more than he did.
The friend didn't get what he meant.
Who were 'these guys'?
But on a closer look, near where he'd been throwing his lunch, there were what looked like the corpses of baby tanuki.
He'd been bringing food to the baby tanuki.{p}

And finally, he died.
Of malnutrition.
Apparently he hadn't been eating anything at home, either.
After that, they say the friend died the same way too.{p}

After that, anyone who went into that restroom died the same way.
So a rumor started.
That if you go into that restroom, something will possess you.
There had already been rumors that the restroom was haunted, so nobody used it anymore.{p}

Ponkichi must have been coming to the school looking for food.
And yet it got shut in by the boy.
So Ponkichi's babies couldn't get food, and they starved to death.
